<!--
The other half of multipanel-notes.qmd. There, every panel carries a label of
its own and is a float in its own right; here the panels are plain code chunks
with a fig-cap and no label, so quarto never marks the figure as having
sub-figures. The two take different paths through floatwithsubfigure.lua and
through quarto's own layout code, and a change that suits one has more than
once broken the other. The .docx note of the whole figure went missing on the
labelled path while this one kept it, which is why nobody noticed for a while:
example.qmd only has this shape.

Base R draws the panels. The point is the layout, not the picture, and a
fixture that pulled in ggplot would take longer to run than everything else
here put together.

A successful run produces, in both formats:

  - Panel labels reading "Panel A" and "Panel B";
  - each panel's own note under that panel;
  - the note of the whole figure under the grid, once;
  - in .docx, the panels side by side in a layout table.
-->

# Method

See @fig-plain.

::: {#fig-plain layout-ncol=2 fig-cap="Two Unlabelled Panels" apa-note="A note belonging to the whole figure."}

```{r}
#| label: leftpanel
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "The left panel."
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-alt: A line.
#| apa-note: "NoNote A note belonging to the left panel."
plot(1:10, type = "l", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
```

```{r}
#| label: rightpanel
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "The right panel."
#| fig-height: 2
#| fig-width: 3
#| fig-alt: Another line.
#| apa-note: "NoNote A note belonging to the right panel."
plot(10:1, type = "l", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
```

:::
